LESSON: GROWING FRUITS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Food Production Processes
Topic 2.2: Growing Fruits

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Growing Fruits. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we grow fruits?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify fruits that can grow the locality

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GROWING FRUITS
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Growing Fruits helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: GROWING FRUITS
Study Growing Fruits like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify fruits that can grow the locality

What this means
In this part you learn to identify fruits that can grow the locality. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify fruits that can grow the locality.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Growing Fruits” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify fruits that can grow the locality. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Growing Fruits is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Growing Fruits” around your school. (skill: identify fruits that can grow the locality)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Growing Fruits to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify fruits that can grow the locality.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Growing Fruits from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Growing Fruits: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Growing Fruits?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we grow fruits?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Growing Fruits means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify fruits that can grow the locality.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
